notes: Sapanca is 1.5 hours from Istanbul (by motorway, or by high-speed train from Arifiye). Explore the lake by car or bike. Maşukiye and Kartepe are 20 minutes away.
It gets very busy on summer weekends, so head to breakfast places before 10:00.
Trout, spread-style breakfast, ıslama köfte (Adapazarı) and chestnuts are local specialities.
Bungalow stays are Sapanca's signature; they cost half as much on weekdays.
The Kartepe summit is cool in summer at around 10°C, so bring a cardigan.
The lakeside path is 5 km long, and the morning mist is lovely for photos.

stops.name: Sapanca Lake Walking Path
stops.tips: A 5 km walking and cycling path along the lake, with morning mist and greenery.

stops.name: Sapanca Lake Pier Cafe
stops.tips: Breakfast and coffee on the lake, on the Kırkpınar shore.

stops.name: Kırkpınar Shore
stops.tips: The liveliest stretch of the lakeshore, with cafes and piers.

stops.name: Sapanca Lake Fish Restaurant
stops.tips: Trout and carp with a view over the lake.

stops.name: Sapanca Lake Sunset Pier
stops.tips: Sunset on the western shore, ideal for photos.

backups.name: Sapanca Bazaar
backups.tips: The town market, good for honey and walnuts.

stops.name: Maşukiye Waterfall
stops.tips: A stream and waterfall at the foot of Kartepe, with walks.

stops.name: Maşukiye Trout Restaurant
stops.tips: Trout and breakfast over the stream, a Maşukiye classic.

stops.name: Maşukiye Village
stops.tips: Village square and market selling walnuts, chestnuts and honey.

stops.name: Kartepe Cable Car
stops.tips: Cable car from Maşukiye up to Kartepe (about 400 TL): highland pasture in summer, snow in winter.

backups.name: Kuzuyayla Nature Park
backups.tips: Forest and picnic spots on the road to Kartepe, an alternative to the cable car.

stops.name: Kartepe Ski Centre
stops.tips: In summer, highland walks at 1,650 m with views of the Gulf of Izmit.

stops.name: Kartepe Summit Restaurant
stops.tips: Sucuk ekmek (spicy sausage in bread) and mantı (Turkish dumplings) at the summit, with a view.

stops.name: Kartepe Hiking Trail
stops.tips: A forest path around the summit; snow walks in winter.

stops.name: Sapanca Evening Bazaar
stops.tips: Stop at the bazaar on the way back for local products.

backups.name: Derbent Gardens
backups.tips: Garden cafes at the foot of Kartepe.

stops.name: Taraklı
stops.tips: One hour from Sapanca: Ottoman houses, Yunus Pasha Mosque and Hıdırlık Hill.

stops.name: Taraklı Mansion Restaurant
stops.tips: Home cooking in a mansion, with uhut (a local stew) and mantı.

stops.name: Taraklı Thermal Baths
stops.tips: A thermal pool, ideal in winter.

stops.name: Adapazarı Bazaar, Sakarya
stops.tips: Stop in Adapazarı on the way back for ıslama köfte (sauce-soaked meatballs).

backups.name: Geyve Gorge
backups.tips: The Sakarya River valley, a scenic alternative to the thermal baths.

stops.name: Poyrazlar Lake
stops.tips: 40 minutes from Sapanca: a lake among sand dunes, with walks.

stops.name: Karasu Beach
stops.tips: A Black Sea beach: swimming in summer, waves in winter.

stops.name: Karasu Fish Restaurant
stops.tips: Black Sea fish and cornbread.

stops.name: Acarlar Floodplain Forest
stops.tips: Subaşı forest with a wooden boardwalk and birdlife.

stops.name: Sapanca Kırkpınar Garden Cafes
stops.tips: Spread-style breakfast in a garden, a Sapanca classic.

stops.name: Sapanca Cycling Tour
stops.tips: Rent a bike and ride around the lake: 20 km of flat road.

stops.name: Mahmudiye Village, Sapanca
stops.tips: The bungalow village, with forest and stream.

stops.name: Mahmudiye Forest Walk
stops.tips: A forest trail above the village, with autumn colours.

days.theme: Lake morning and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Sapanca Lake Morning Walk
stops.tips: One last walk along the lake.

stops.name: Sapanca Market Square
stops.tips: Friday market (or the bazaar if there isn't one): honey, walnuts and chestnuts.

stops.name: Sapanca Seaside Breakfast Place
stops.tips: A farewell breakfast.

backups.name: Sapanca Lakeside Tea Garden
backups.tips: Tea and toasted sandwiches by the lake, a fitting goodbye.
